issues.display_title: Issue #121: Add global user role + support-only authorization guard
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Global User Role and Support Authorization Guard (Task #121 / PR #129 )

Overview

This task adds a global user role for support authorization. The role is separate from project-level owner, editor, and viewer permissions.

Code Implementation

  1. Global User Role (src/models/models.go):

    • Added Role to models.User as varchar(20) with NOT NULL and an empty-string default.
    • Kept the global role independent from ProjectMember.Role.
    • Existing and unknown role values remain non-support unless they exactly equal support.

  2. Database Migration (migrations/202608100001_add_users_role.sql):

    • Adds public.users.role using ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS.
    • Uses NOT NULL DEFAULT '' so existing rows are backfilled safely and fresh/existing database schemas match.

  3. Support Authorization Middleware (src/middleware/auth.go):

    • Added middleware.SupportOnly().
    • Returns 401 Unauthorized when no authenticated user exists in the request context.
    • Allows access only when middleware.GetUser(c).Role == "support".
    • Returns 403 Forbidden for empty, unknown, non-support, or project-level role values.
    • Reads the role only from the database-backed authenticated user loaded by middleware.Auth(); no request body or JWT role is trusted.

  4. Current User Response (src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go):

    • Added role to the existing GET /v1/auth/me user response.
    • Existing response fields remain unchanged.

Testing

src/middleware/auth_test.go covers:

  • Exact support role passes.
  • Non-support role returns 403.
  • Empty role returns 403.
  • Unknown or differently-cased role returns 403.
  • Project owner role returns 403.
  • Missing authenticated user returns 401.

Security Decision

The role is deliberately excluded from JWT claims. middleware.Auth() loads the current user row on every request, so role changes and revocations take effect immediately instead of remaining valid for the session token's 30-day lifetime.

Verification

go build ./...
go vet ./...

Both commands pass. Test execution on the local Windows environment is blocked by Application Control when Go attempts to launch generated test executables; PR review verification reports the middleware and route tests passing.

PRD #120 (Support Feedback Management API). FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

There is no global role concept in this repo. models.User (src/models/models.go:27) has no role field, and ProjectMember roles (owner/editor/viewer) are per-project only. The support inbox endpoints in #120 need a global support role plus one centralized guard.

Why

Every support endpoint (#120 sections 4–7) is gated on this. Without a single fail-closed helper, the guard gets re-implemented per route and one of them ends up wrong.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Role field on models.User — varchar(20), default empty string
  • SQL migration migrations/<ts>_add_users_role.sql adding the column (AutoMigrate covers fresh DBs; explicit SQL keeps existing CockroachDB deploys in sync — same pattern as 202607240001_add_project_invitations.sql)
  • middleware.SupportOnly() — passes only when middleware.GetUser(c).Role == "support", exact match
  • Fails closed: missing, empty, or unknown role → 403
  • Role is never read from the request body or any client-controlled input
  • Project owner/editor/viewer grants no support access
  • GET /v1/auth/me returns role (src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go) — additive, existing fields unchanged
  • Tests: support → pass, non-support → 403, empty role → 403, unknown role → 403, unauthenticated → 401, project owner → 403
  • src/routes/v1/role_matrix_test.go and existing auth/login/me tests still green

Scope decision — role stays out of the JWT

The PRD asks for the global role to be embedded in issued JWTs. Descoped deliberately, do not implement.

middleware.Auth() (src/middleware/auth.go:37-40) already loads the full user row from the database on every request, so GetUser(c).Role is available with no token change. Meanwhile SessionTokenTTL is 30 days (src/utils/jwt.go:12) — a role baked into the token would keep revoked support access alive for up to 30 days after the role is removed.

Dependencies

None. Blocks all other #120 tasks.

issues.display_title: Issue #127: Backfill createdAt on the new accessPoints canvas array (FE #585)
issues.main_description_html:
The frontend shipped a new canvas object array, accessPoints (FE gothru-3d-floorplan#585, merged to development). StampCanvasCreatedAt does not know about it yet, so access markers never get the server-owned createdAt backfill every other object kind gets.

Background

Access (lifts and stairs) used to be an area — an AreaLayer whose type was "lift" or "stairs". It is now its own point object, stored per level as:

{
  "levels": [
    {
      "level_id": "L1",
      "accessPoints": [
        { "id": "a1", "x": 120, "y": 340, "accessId": "g1", "type": "lift",
          "name": "Main lift", "infoId": "i9", "createdAt": 1786... }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

Storage needs no change — StampCanvasCreatedAt walks the blob as generic JSON (map[string]any), so the new key already round-trips untouched. That was verified while writing this; it is only the createdAt backfill that is missing.

The change

src/action/v1/shared/createdat.go — add one entry to canvasObjectPaths:

var canvasObjectPaths = [][]string{
	{"layout", "walls"},
	{"layout", "areas"},
	{"floorplanMeta", "doors"},
	{"floorplanMeta", "windows"},
	{"shapes"},
	{"points"},
	{"safetyAnnotations"},
	{"accessPoints"},   // <- new (FE #585)
	{"panoramas"},
}

That is the whole change. The file's own comment already anticipates it: "only a brand-new object ARRAY needs a line here."

Why it matters

createdAt is what orders the editor's object list newest-first (FE #392). An access marker that reaches the server without one keeps none, so it sorts as the oldest object forever — it sinks to the bottom of the list no matter when the user drew it.

That is not hypothetical: the frontend has a known bug where a marker placed right after a level loads is not stamped client-side (levelToModel hands the engine the store's own array by reference, so the object is already in prev when the stamp is decided). The server backfill is exactly the safety net for that case, which is why every other object array is listed.

Acceptance Criteria

  • {"accessPoints"} added to canvasObjectPaths
  • A level whose accessPoints[] objects have no createdAt comes back with each stamped 1 (unknownCreatedAt), matching the existing behaviour for points / safetyAnnotations
  • An existing createdAt on an access point is never overwritten
  • Unknown fields on an access point (accessId, type, name, infoId, accessOriginLevelId) still round-trip untouched
  • Test added in src/action/v1/shared/createdat_test.go alongside the existing per-array cases
  • go test ./... green

Assigned to: Pebi Sandi Pratama — Backend Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #122: Add feedback + feedback reply models and migration
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Feedback Models and Migration (Task #122 / PR #130 )

Overview

This task adds the persistence layer for user feedback and support reply history. Identity and project names are stored as snapshots so records remain readable after users or projects change.

Code Implementation

  1. Feedback Model (src/models/models.go):

    • Added Feedback with a generated UUID, submitting user identity snapshots, optional project context, feedback content, workflow state, internal notes, and timestamps.
    • status defaults to new.
    • internal_notes defaults to an empty string and cannot be NULL.
    • project_id and project_name use pointers because both fields are optional.
    • Added indexes for status, category, area, project ID, creation time, and update time.

  2. Feedback Reply Model (src/models/models.go):

    • Added FeedbackReply with a generated UUID, feedback ID, sender identity snapshots, recipient email snapshot, message, and creation time.
    • Added an index on feedback_id.
    • Replies are exposed through the Feedback.Replies association.

  3. Model Registration (src/models/models.go):

    • Registered Feedback and FeedbackReply in models.AllModels() for fresh database AutoMigrate runs.

  4. SQL Migration (migrations/202608100002_add_feedback.sql):

    • Creates public.feedbacks and public.feedback_replies with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.
    • Creates all required indexes with CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS.
    • Uses migration version 202608100002, after task #121 migration 202608100001.
    • Statements are idempotent for fresh and existing databases.

Testing

src/models/models_test.go verifies:

  • Both models migrate successfully.
  • Repeated AutoMigrate succeeds.
  • Feedback and reply UUIDs are generated.
  • Feedback status defaults to new.
  • Both models are registered in AllModels().

Verification

go test ./src/models -count=1
go test ./cmd/migrate -count=1
go test ./src/routes/v1 -run TestProjectWriteEndpointsRoleMatrix -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...

All commands pass.

PRD #120 (Support Feedback Management API). FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

Persistence layer for user feedback and support replies. No feedback tables or models exist today.

Why

Every #120 endpoint reads or writes these two tables. Landing the schema first keeps the endpoint tasks parallel.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Feedback model in src/models/models.go: ID, submitting user ID, user name snapshot, user email snapshot, optional project ID, optional project name, area, path, category, rating, comment, status, internal notes, submitted_at, created_at, updated_at
  • Status defaults to new at the model level

  • Both registered in models.AllModels()
  • SQL migration migrations/<ts>_add_feedback.sql creating both tables (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, same style as 202607240001_add_project_invitations.sql)
  • Indexes on status, category, area, project_id, created_at, updated_at
  • Index on feedback_replies.feedback_id
  • Migration runs clean on a fresh database and on an existing one

Dependencies

#121 (global role) — merge first to avoid migration ordering conflicts.

RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Feedback Submission API (Task #123 / PR #134 )

Overview

This task adds POST /v1/feedback for authenticated users. The endpoint validates feedback, stores immutable user snapshots, and creates each record with status new.

Code Implementation

  1. Feedback Action (src/action/v1/feedback/create.go):

    • Parses required fields: area, category, rating, comment, path, and submitted_at.
    • Accepts optional project_id and project_name.
    • Accepts categories bug, confusing, missing, slow, and praise, matching the frontend contract.
    • Restricts ratings to values from 1 through 5.
    • Reads user ID, name, and email from middleware.GetUser(c); client-provided identity fields are ignored.
    • Persists the feedback using one DB.Create call.
    • Returns 201 with the generated feedback ID and status new.
    • Returns 400 for invalid payloads and 500 for persistence failures.

  2. Controller and Route:

    • Added the feedback controller under src/controllers/v1/feedback.
    • Registered POST /v1/feedback in src/routes/v1/feedback.go.
    • Applies middleware.Auth() only; SupportOnly() is intentionally not used because normal authenticated users submit feedback.
    • Registered feedback routes in src/routes/routes.go.

  3. API Collection (api-collection/v1/feedback):

    • Added the feedback folder and authenticated submission request.
    • Included a complete payload example and validation constraints.

Testing

Tests cover:

  • Successful submission with status new.
  • Authenticated user ID, name, and email snapshots.
  • Client-controlled user ID rejection.
  • Submission with and without project context.
  • Every missing required field returning 400.
  • Invalid category and rating returning 400.
  • Unauthenticated requests returning 401.
  • Isolated in-memory databases per test so shuffled execution cannot leak rows between tests.

Verification

go test ./src/action/v1/feedback -shuffle=on -count=15
go test ./src/action/v1/feedback -count=3
go build ./...
go vet ./...

All commands pass.

PRD #120 section 3. FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

Endpoint any authenticated user calls to submit feedback. This is the only feedback route that is not support-gated — it takes middleware.Auth() only.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/feedback registered with middleware.Auth() and no SupportOnly guard
  • Required fields validated: area, category, rating, comment, path, submitted_at
  • Optional fields accepted: project_id, project_name
  • Stores authenticated user's UniqueID from middleware.GetUser(c) — user ID is never taken from the request body
  • Stores user name and email snapshots at submit time
  • Single database write
  • 201 with feedback ID and status new

  • Tests: valid payload → 201 + status new + tied to authed user; snapshots stored; works with and without project context; each missing required field → 400; invalid category → 400; invalid rating → 400; unauthenticated → 401
  • api-collection/v1/feedback entry added

#122 (models). Guard helper from #121 not needed here.

issues.display_title: Issue #124: Implement support feedback list + detail endpoints
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback List and Detail API (Task #124)

Overview

This task adds the support inbox read API: a searchable, filterable, deterministically sorted feedback list and a complete feedback detail endpoint. Both routes require authentication and the exact global support role.

Endpoints

  • GET /v1/support/feedback
  • GET /v1/support/feedback/:id

The list deliberately lives under /v1/support/feedback, keeping all support routes behind one middleware group while /v1/feedback remains the authenticated user submission route.

Code Implementation

  1. Support Route Group (src/routes/v1/feedback.go):

    • Added a /support/feedback group protected by middleware.Auth() and middleware.SupportOnly().
    • Registered list and detail routes on that group.
    • Unauthenticated requests return 401; authenticated non-support users return 403.

  2. Feedback List (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Supports search, status, category, area, project_id, and sort query parameters.
    • Validates statuses against new, reviewing, replied, resolved, and closed.
    • Validates sort modes against newest, oldest, recently_updated, and status.
    • Filters use fixed server-owned column names and bound query values.
    • Search matches comment, user email, project name, area, category, and path case-insensitively.
    • Escapes backslash, %, and _, preventing user input from becoming unintended SQL LIKE wildcards.
    • Preloads reply history in deterministic creation order.

  3. Deterministic Sorting (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • newest: creation time descending.
    • oldest: creation time ascending.
    • recently_updated: update time descending.
    • status: workflow order new, reviewing, replied, resolved, closed.
    • Every mode adds id ASC as a stable tie-breaker.

  4. Feedback Detail (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Loads one complete feedback record by ID.
    • Includes full comment, user snapshots, optional project context, status, internal notes, timestamps, and reply history.
    • Returns 404 for an unknown ID and 500 for database failures.

  5. Response Contract (src/action/v1/feedback/read.go):

    • Uses a support-specific response type.
    • Exposes internal notes as notes, matching the support API contract.
    • List responses use data.feedback as an array; detail responses use data.feedback as one object.

  6. Controller and API Collection:

    • Added list and detail forwarding methods to the feedback controller.
    • Added API collection requests for both support endpoints.

Testing

src/action/v1/feedback/read_test.go covers:

  • Support user receives feedback records.
  • Status, category, area, and project filters.
  • Search across all six required fields.
  • Literal % and _ search behavior.
  • All four deterministic sort modes.
  • Workflow status order including closed.
  • Invalid status and sort values returning 400.
  • Detail response containing notes and reply history.
  • Unknown ID returning 404.
  • Isolated in-memory databases for reliable shuffled execution.

src/routes/v1/support_feedback_test.go covers:

  • Support access returning 200.
  • Non-support access returning 403.
  • Unauthenticated access returning 401.

Scope Decisions

  • Pagination remains outside task #124 and can be added later without breaking the response contract.
  • Malformed UUID handling follows existing repository behavior and is not changed by this task.

Verification

go test ./src/action/v1/feedback ./src/routes/v1 -count=1
go build ./...
go vet ./...

All commands pass.

PRD #120 sections 4–5. FE counterpart: GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578.

Description

Support inbox read side: filtered/sorted list plus single-record detail. Both SupportOnly.

Route change vs PRD — read before coding

The PRD puts the list at GET /v1/feedback while detail/update/reply sit under /v1/support/feedback/:id. That would make /v1/feedback carry two different guards depending on HTTP method (POST = any authed user, GET = support only), which is easy to get wrong when the route group applies middleware.

Decision: list moves to GET /v1/support/feedback. All support routes then live under one group with one guard, and /v1/feedback stays POST-only for users.

This is a contract change for the frontend — GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#578 must use /v1/support/feedback for the list.

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v1/support/feedback and GET /v1/support/feedback/:id, both behind middleware.Auth() + SupportOnly()
  • Query params: search, status, category, area, project_id, sort
  • search matches comment, user email, project name, area, category, and path
  • status validated against new, reviewing, replied, resolved, closed
  • sort validated against newest, oldest, recently_updated, status
  • Sorting is deterministic — every sort mode gets a stable ID tie-breaker
  • List returns user identity, project context, feedback content, status, notes, replies, timestamps
  • Detail returns full comment, status, internal notes, user identity, project context, timestamps, and reply history
  • Errors: 401 unauthenticated, 403 non-support, 400 invalid status or sort value, 404 unknown ID (detail), 500
  • Tests: support user gets records; each filter returns only matching rows; search hits all six fields; each sort mode deterministic; invalid status → 400; invalid sort → 400; unknown ID → 404; non-support → 403; unauthenticated → 401
  • api-collection/v1 entries added

Dependencies

#121 (SupportOnly guard), #122 (models).

RESULT 10/08/26

✅ Implementation: Support Feedback Update API (Task #125 / PR #137 )

Overview

This task adds a support-only endpoint for updating a feedback record's workflow status and internal notes.

Endpoint

The route uses the existing /support/feedback group protected by middleware.Auth() and middleware.SupportOnly().

  2. Response Contract:

    • Returns the feedback ID, status, internal notes as notes, and refreshed updated_at.
    • Internal notes remain confined to support-facing endpoints.

  3. Controller and Route:

    • Registered PATCH /v1/support/feedback/:id on the existing authenticated support group.
    • Unauthenticated requests return 401; authenticated non-support users return 403.

  4. API Collection (api-collection/v1/feedback/Update support feedback.yml):

    • Added an authenticated PATCH example containing both status and notes.
    • Documents that at least one update field is required.

Testing

src/action/v1/feedback/update_test.go covers:

  • Status-only update.
  • Notes-only update.
  • Combined status and notes update.
  • Every valid workflow status.
  • Invalid status returning 400.
  • Empty update body returning 400.
  • Unknown feedback ID returning 404.
  • Refreshed updated_at after a successful update.

src/routes/v1/support_feedback_test.go additionally verifies that a non-support user receives 403 from the PATCH route.

Verification

go build ./...
go vet ./...

All commands pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #131: Duplicate project: owner-only POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate (row + files + blobs, copy is a draft)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Add POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate — an owner-only endpoint that forks a project into a fully independent copy.

  • Owner only. Stricter than publish/unpublish/delete (which accept role.CanWrite()): an editor member may change a project but may not fork it into a new project they would own. Non-owner → 403 via members.Forbidden(project).
  • Copy the row. Every column of projects is copied except: new id, freshly generated unique project_key, name = "{name} - copy", status = "draft", last_opened_at = NULL.
  • Never inherit publish state. Duplicating a published project must not publish the copy — the copy is a draft on a brand-new share key, so the original's /v/{key} link is untouched and the copy has no public link until its owner publishes it.
  • Copy the files. Every project_files row is recreated under the new project id and every stored blob is physically copied — both storage drivers (local disk under STORAGE_PATH/<projectId>/ and MinIO under the <projectId>/ object prefix). File names are kept identical, so every fileName reference inside the copied JSON blobs still resolves.
  • Re-point the JSON blobs. The frontend bakes the project id into stored file references — floor_configs[].serverPath (minio:///<projectId>/<file>) and the /api/files?projectId=<id>&name=… URLs inside information_records and generated_twins. Since file names are unchanged, swapping the source id for the new id inside floor_configs, generated_twins, canvas_data, information_records and categories re-points all of them. Everything else in those blobs is a nanoid, which never contains a project uuid.
  • Members / invitations are NOT copied. The duplicate belongs to the owner alone until they share it.
  • Failure after the row is created rolls the duplicate back (DeleteProject).

Why

There is no way to branch off an existing project today — the only path is rebuilding a floor plan from scratch. Users want to try changes, produce a variant of a venue, or keep a snapshot before a big edit, without touching the published original.

Doing this on the backend rather than orchestrating create + PATCH + re-upload from the frontend is the only way to copy the stored blobs at all: the FE has no list-files endpoint, and re-uploading would mint new file names and break every reference in the JSON.

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /v1/projects/:id/duplicate returns 201 with the standard project response for the copy
  • Only the owner may call it — an editor member gets 403 with the owner-naming body, and no copy is created
  • Unknown id → 404; unauthenticated → 401
  • Copy has a new id, a new unique project_key, name = "{original} - copy", status = "draft" — including when the original is published
  • All content columns are copied: canvas_data, floor_configs, generated_twins, information_records, categories, active_level_id, canvas_filter, map_style, floor_image_opacity, description, location_*, is_complete
  • Every project_files row is recreated for the copy, with file_url re-pointed at the new project id
  • Every stored blob is physically copied under the new project id, on both the local-disk and MinIO drivers
  • Stored file paths inside the copied blobs point at the copy, not the original
  • Editing the copy (row, blobs or files) leaves the original completely untouched, and vice versa
  • Build + tests green

Dependencies

None. FE counterpart (dashboard "Duplicate" menu item + duplicateProject server action) ships on gothru-3d-floormap and depends on this endpoint.

RESULT

Implemented on feature/131-duplicate-project, commit 30a009e, merged to development via PR #132 (f739d7c).

Files

  • src/action/v1/project/duplicate.go (new) — Duplicate handler, copyProjectFiles, copyProjectBlob, repointProjectBlobs
  • src/controllers/v1/project/duplicate.go (new)
  • src/routes/v1/projects.go — projects.Post("/:id/duplicate", pc.Duplicate)
  • src/action/v1/project/duplicate_test.go (new)

How it works

  • Loads the project, resolves the caller's role with members.FetchRoleForProject, and rejects anything but RoleOwner with members.Forbidden(project) — stricter than publish/delete's CanWrite(), so an editor member cannot fork a project.
  • Copies the row struct wholesale, then resets Base, ProjectKey, Files, sets name = "{name} - copy", status = "draft", last_opened_at = NULL, and creates it through the existing createProjectWithGeneratedKey retry helper so the copy gets its own unique share key.
  • copyProjectFiles recreates every project_files row under the new id with file_url re-pointed, and copyProjectBlob physically copies each blob — ReadObject/PutObject for MinIO, io.Copy into STORAGE_PATH/<newId>/ for local disk — keeping identical file names so all fileName references stay valid.
  • repointProjectBlobs swaps the source id for the new id inside floor_configs, generated_twins, canvas_data, information_records and categories, which covers the two places the FE bakes the project id into stored references: floor_configs[].serverPath (minio:///<projectId>/<file>) and the /api/files?projectId=<id>&name= URLs in information records. Exact because file names are unchanged; every other id in those blobs is a nanoid.
  • Any failure after the row exists rolls the duplicate back with DeleteProject.
  • Members and invitations are deliberately not copied — the duplicate belongs to the owner alone until they share it.

Tests

  • TestDuplicateCopiesEverythingAsADraft — a published original yields a - copy draft with a new key, the blob and file row are copied, serverPath is re-pointed at the new id, and editing the copy (row + blob) leaves the original untouched.
  • TestDuplicateIsOwnerOnly — an editor member gets 403 and no second project row is created.

go build ./... and go vet ./src/... clean. go test ./... green except src/action/v1/predict (TestPredictStreamsSSEEvents), which already fails on development and is unrelated to this change.

FE counterpart — gothru-3d-floormap: duplicateProject server action + dashboard "Duplicate" menu item behind the existing owner guard.
